_comment: Blogs the research agent watches. SIGNAL sources — timing and gaps — not topic lists to copy. Notes below include Iván's own read on each plus what a manual crawl (July 27, 2026) actually found. Run `python3 research_agent.py --check-sources` on the VPS to verify the feed guesses before the first real run.

sources.name: TrainingPeaks — Training Articles
sources.note: WordPress, but /blog/feed/ redirects to an article instead of serving XML — verified manually, hence html mode. Your own marketplace's audience, so highest relevance AND the one competitor you must not attack head-on: you will not outrank them on their strong topics.

sources.name: TrainingPeaks — Coach Blog
sources.note: Coach-facing. Doubles as source material for the LinkedIn solo-operator track.

sources.name: TrainRight (CTS)
sources.note: Carmichael Training Systems. High-volume, broad endurance coverage. Big authority — treat as a gap-finder, not a topic list.

sources.name: High North Performance
sources.note: Squarespace. IMPORTANT: editorially dormant — last article April 2024, most are 2023. Iván's aesthetic reference (see brand-guidelines.md §1) and now a content reference too, but it produces no timing signal. Value is its ARCHIVE as a topic map, and its 'Paper Review' format, which is worth stealing as a format. Cycling only; they run a separate running site at highnorthrunning.co.uk.

sources.name: High North Running
sources.note: The running arm of High North — added because the main site is cycling-only and Iván's catalog is running-heavy (195 of 323 published plans).

sources.name: MyProCoach
sources.note: Structured plan seller, closest business model to the plans catalog. Watch for how they position plans vs coaching.

sources.name: Stryd
sources.note: Ghost CMS, so /rss/ should work. Crawled manually: mostly elite athlete race recaps, 'Inside the Data' race analyses, monthly workout drops and firmware notes — brand marketing, not evergreen education. Low value as a topic source. HIGH value for two other reasons: Iván is a Stryd coach and has power-based plans, making this the clearest affiliate fit; and 'Inside the Data' is a format worth adapting with his own athletes' files.

sources.name: EndureIQ
sources.note: Dr Dan Plews. Iván: 'they gate a lot of content but they are GOOD.' The clearest working example of the gated_teaser model we're copying — study how much they give away before the gate.

sources.name: Dr Will O'Connor
sources.note: Iván: more active on YouTube than the blog. Expect a thin feed; the real signal is on video, which this agent does not read. Consider adding a YouTube RSS feed later (youtube.com/feeds/videos.xml?channel_id=...).

sources.name: Higher Running
sources.note: Closest business analogue — solo-ish coaching + plans + newsletter, started ~10 years ago. Crawled manually: their 'blog' is a NEWSLETTER ARCHIVE, not SEO content. Titles are subject lines ('You're within 5 minutes of a sub-3 hour marathon'), not search queries, and roughly half are athlete transformation stories. They monetize through relationship and story, not search. Publishing ~1-2/month, irregular. This is the strongest argument for adding case_study as an article type.

settings._languages_note: PT ideas must stay inside the distances that actually have PT inventory — marathon, 5k, 10k, 21k, FTP. Everything else points at plans that don't exist.
settings._dormant_sources_note: High North last published April 2024. The agent must not treat an old post as a current signal — that's what lookback_days is for. Its archive is still useful as a topic map, so it stays in the list, but expect zero recent posts from it.
